scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C - D
scalesUsed.application: Primary harmonic framework providing the flattened 7th (C natural) that creates the signature hard-rock groove without classical leading-tone stiffness

scalesUsed.notes: D - F - G - G# - A - C - D
scalesUsed.application: Lead guitar fills and Angus Young's fiery solo work, utilizing the blues diminished fifth (G#) and minor third (F) over the major tonic

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - A - B - D
scalesUsed.application: Sweet melodic phrasing in the intro theme and resolution lines, emphasizing the major third (F#) and sixth (B)

keyAndScale.keySignature: 2 sharps (F#, C#) - modified to C natural in Mixolydian

mainProgression.description: Signature driving groove combining D tonic with Mixolydian ♭VII (C5) and first-inversion subdominant (G/B) resolving back to tonic D

sectionProgressions.description: Syncopated pedal riff by Angus Young over driving straight eighth-note bass and four-on-the-floor kick
Punchy downstroke rhythm pattern with syncopated stops locking directly with the rhythm section
Aggressive blues-rock modal borrowing using the ♭III (F5) power chord to escalate vocal and harmonic tension
Driving Mixolydian vamp providing the harmonic foundation for Angus's high-register triplet runs and expressive bends

harmonicFunction: D5 (I) - Anchors the track with an unwavering tonic tonal center and powerful low-end resonance
C5 (♭VII) - Borrowed from D Mixolydian, eliminating the classical leading-tone to produce pure rock attitude and drive
G5/B (IV/6) - Subdominant chord with B in the bass, smoothing the voice leading between C and D
F5 (♭III) - Borrowed from D Aeolian/Blues, injecting gritty tension into the explosive chorus shout

techniques.name: Syncopated Open-String Pedal Riffing
techniques.description: Angus Young's signature intro motif combining open D-string pedal notes with syncopated double-stops and hammer-ons on the G and B strings

notes: Keep the open D string ringing cleanly as a rhythmic anchor
Use quick hammer-ons and pull-offs between the 5th and 7th frets on the G string
Accent the offbeat eighth notes to match Simon Wright's kick groove
Maintain strict wrist control without letting excess strings ring out
sequence: Strike open D string with solid downstroke attack
Fret 7th fret D (G string) and hammer from 5th fret
Shift to 8th fret B string for high tonic punch
Resolve back to D root with slight vibrato
tips: Practice with a metronome at 90 BPM before pushing to the record tempo of 128 BPM
Use the flesh of your fretting index finger to lightly mute the low E and A strings
Focus on rhythmic bounce rather than brute picking force

techniques.name: Locked-In Downstroke Power Chords
techniques.description: Malcolm Young's rock-solid rhythm foundation featuring tight, uncompressed downstrokes with precision palm muting and rhythmic rests

notes: D5: X-X-0-2-3-X (Open D with 2nd fret G and 3rd fret B)
C5: X-3-5-5-X-X (3rd fret A string power chord)
G5/B: X-2-0-0-3-3 or X-2-5-X-X-X (1st inversion G chord voice-leading to D)
F5: 1-3-3-X-X-X (1st fret low E power chord for chorus punch)
Execute sharp staccato cutoffs using the fretting hand release
sequence: Attack D5 with heavy downstroke on the downbeat
Mute immediately on the following upbeat for clean rhythmic space
Anticipate C5 on the upbeat of beat 4
Step down through G5/B before hammering back into D5
tips: Use medium-heavy picks (1.0mm+) for crisp attack and dynamic punch
Keep the right hand wrist relaxed to maintain stamina throughout the song
Do not over-distort: Malcolm's tone is famously clean and articulate

techniques.name: Mixolydian & Blues Scale Lead Hybrid
techniques.description: Angus Young's fluid transition between major pentatonic sweetness and aggressive minor pentatonic blues biting bends

notes: Position 1 D minor pentatonic: 10th-13th frets on B and high E strings
Full whole-step bends on the 12th fret G string (bending G to A)
Overbending on the 13th fret B string (C bending up toward D)
Wide, singing vibrato applied at the peak of bent notes
sequence: Enter solo on the 10th fret high E string
Execute whole-step bend on 13th fret B string with index finger reinforcement
Descend through D blues scale hitting the 11th fret G# blue note
Resolve to 12th fret D string tonic with aggressive vibrato
tips: Support bends with your index and middle fingers behind the ring finger
Listen to the vocal phrasing of Brian Johnson to mimic vocal inflection
Control feedback organically using volume and guitar position relative to the amp
details.progression: Over D5 - C5 - G5 - D5 backing track

sections.name: Intro Theme Riff
sections.description: Angus Young's iconic single-note syncopated intro establishing the danceable rock tempo and modal D center
notes: Open D string acts as a ringing pedal note throughout the phrase
Accent the syncopated hammer-ons on beats 2 and 4
Keep the rhythm crisp and in the pocket with the straight 4-on-the-floor kick
Dynamic crescendo leading into the full band entry at 0:30

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Punchy verse groove driven by Malcolm Young's signature rhythm precision with D5, C5, and G/B
notes: Use exclusively downstrokes for heavy attack and consistent tonal weight
Release fretting pressure immediately after striking to create staccato spaces
The C5 chord anticipates the beat for irresistible forward momentum
Bass voice leading moves cleanly: D -> C -> B -> D

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Explosive vocal hook backed by the heavy D5 - F5 - G5 - D5 chord sequence featuring the borrowed flat-third (F5)
notes: F5 power chord at the 1st fret low E string injects dark blues-rock grit
Full band vocal gang shouts answer the rhythm stabs
Let chords ring slightly longer than verse staccatos for wall-of-sound resonance
Solid transition back to the verse riff via open D strike
sections.exerciseLabel: Chorus Power Chords & Modal Borrow Exercise

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Angus Young takes center stage with a soaring, blues-drenched guitar solo featuring rapid triplet runs and screaming bends
notes: Solo starts in 10th fret box of D minor pentatonic
Aggressive whole-step bends on B string at 13th fret
Combines blues grit with clean rhythmic syncopation
High E string sustain with expressive, fast finger vibrato

guitar.recommended: Gibson SG Standard (1968) / Gretsch G6131 Jet Firebird
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker with moderate vintage output (Gibson PAF / T-Top or Gretsch Filter'Tron)

effects.distortion: Amp overdrive driven by master volume; no overdrive/distortion pedals used
effects.reverb: Natural room acoustics from Compass Point Studios, Nassau
effects.other: Schaffer-Vega Diversity System (SVDS) wireless unit for midrange boost, companding, and clean preamp punch

beginner.title: Rhythm Fundamentals
steps: Master the D5, C5, and G5/B power chord hand grips
Practice downstroke muting and staccato cutoffs with a metronome at 100 BPM
Memorize the verse chord sequence (D5 - C5 - G5/B - D5)

intermediate.title: Groove & Intro Theme
steps: Lock in Angus Young's syncopated intro riff at full tempo (128 BPM)
Smoothly transition between the verse rhythm and the F5 chorus modal borrow
Coordinate fretting-hand cutoffs with the four-on-the-floor kick drum pulse

advanced.title: Angus Young Solo Mastery
steps: Execute rapid-fire D minor pentatonic triplet pull-offs in position 1
Master accurate whole-step and minor-third bends on the 13th fret B string
Develop Angus's wide, vocal-like hand vibrato on sustained lead notes

commonMistakes: Using too much amplifier distortion, which causes the syncopated chord spaces to sound muddy instead of punchy
Rushing the offbeat C5 chord entry before Simon Wright's snare hits on beats 2 and 4
Allowing unused strings to vibrate during Angus's intro pedal riff
Playing the chorus F5 with sloppy finger positioning, resulting in buzzing on the 1st fret
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: Angus intro theme practice at 90, 110, and 128 BPM with a metronome
10 minutes: Malcolm downstroke power chord endurance drill over the D5 - C5 - G/B - D5 verse groove
10 minutes: Chorus modal borrow transitions (D5 to F5 to G5 to D5)
15 minutes: Guitar solo lick isolation and whole-step bend pitch accuracy work
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM to nail the exact note values and staccato rests of the verse groove
Increase by 4 BPM increments every 3 clean repetitions until reaching 128 BPM
Practice muting all strings exactly on beat 2 and 4 for high-impact rhythmic tightness
